title: The Shundai Zatsuwa (A Japanese Philosopher)
author: muro-kyuso
attributionNote: Murō Kyūsō (1658–1734) compiled the Shundai zatsuwa from the conversations of his teacher Dazai Shundai and his own notes; the book records the teaching of the Japanese school of Ancient Learning, which read the Confucian texts without the Neo-Confucian commentaries.
description: The Shundai Zatsuwa is the record of a Japanese Confucian teacher's talk on the five virtues: benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom and sincerity. Its five books argue that the way of the Chinese sages is the way for Japan, attack Buddhist and Daoist claims, and describe the duties of the samurai and of government. It is the clearest English window on the school of Ancient Learning in Tokugawa Japan.
historicalContext: The text was translated by George William Knox and printed in the Transactions of the Asiatic Society of Japan in 1892, and it was this version that the archive transcribed. Its Confucianism is Japanese and Tokugawa: the same classics read in a society organised around warriors and daimyo.
availabilityNote: Complete: the five books on the virtues, streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one book per chapter. The translator's introduction, a separate essay on Japanese Neo-Confucian thought, is not part of the work.
